# Ontology Builder — Feature Extraction

Every feature below was read out of the reference platforms' **source code**, not their marketing material. Each carries the exact service, handler, enum or extension point it came from, so the port can be checked against the original.

**Totals:** 141 features across 22 areas, mapping to 42 of 44 capabilities in the Ontology Engineering Capability Model.

## 1. Sources

| ID | Platform | Repository | Stack | Licence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `VB3` | **VocBench 3 / Semantic Turkey** | `bitbucket.org/art-uniroma2/vocbench3 (+ semanticturkey, auth-walled)` | Angular 1x SPA · Java 11 · Spring + OSGi (Apache Karaf) · RDF4J · file-based project/user store · tuProlog + jsprolog authorization | BSD-3 / academic (Univ. Roma Tor Vergata, EU Publications Office) |
| `WP` | **WebProtégé** | `github.com/protegeproject/webprotege (+ ~15 microservice repos)` | GWT 2.8 client (MVP) · Java servlets · Dagger 2 · MongoDB · Lucene · OWL API 4.5 · migrating to Spring Boot microservices + Keycloak + RabbitMQ | BSD-2 |
| `PD` | **Protégé Desktop** | `github.com/protegeproject/protege` | Java Swing · OSGi (Equinox/Felix) · OWL API · HermiT/ELK/Pellet/FaCT++ | BSD-2 |

**VocBench 3 / Semantic Turkey.** The reference implementation for *controlled collaborative editing*: multi-project, RBAC-with-validation, triple-level history, staging graphs.

**WebProtégé.** The reference implementation for *web-scale project sharing*: capability/role authorization, axiom-level revision history, declarative forms, perspectives/portlets, watches and threaded comments.

**Protégé Desktop.** The reference implementation for *deep OWL authoring*: Manchester-syntax class expression editing, DL reasoning with explanations, refactoring operations, and a 24-extension-point plugin architecture.

## 3. Feature catalogue

### PRJ · Project & Workspace Management

*The project as the unit of work, configuration, isolation and access.*  ·  Backend package `ontology_builder.projects`

#### OB.PRJ.01 · Project registry & lifecycle  `[MUST]` `[P0]`

Create, list, open, close, delete and describe projects; a project is the unit of configuration, access control, history and release.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · Projects.createProject/deleteProject/listProjects/accessProject/disconnectFromProject (52 ops in Projects service)<br>**WP** · CreateNewProjectActionHandler, LoadProjectActionHandler, GetAvailableProjectsWithPermissionActionHandler, MoveProjectsToTrash
- **Capabilities:** B.SG.2 Ontology Governance & Stewardship, B.SE.3 Use-Case & Requirements Management, T.OO.1 Triplestore & Ontology Storage
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.projects.registry`
- **Reuse existing:** `src/Ontology Modeler/ontology_modeler/config.py`
- **Note:** VB3 `Project` carries name, baseURI, defaultNamespace, model, lexicalizationModel, open, visibility, readOnly, history/validation/blacklisting/undo/shacl/trivialInference flags, facets, labels.

#### OB.PRJ.02 · Semantic model & lexicalization model declaration  `[MUST]` `[P0]`

Each project declares a core model (OWL | SKOS | SKOS-XL | OntoLex) and an independent lexicalization model (RDFS | SKOS | SKOS-XL | OntoLex); the UI, the tree set and the validation rules follow from the pair.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · Project.model + Project.lexicalizationModel; §4.1.3 of the SWJ paper
- **Capabilities:** T.DA.2 Ontology Formalization (OWL/RDFS/SKOS), T.DA.6 Vocabulary & Controlled-Term Management, T.AC.5 Multilingual & Localization Support
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.projects.model_profile`
- **Depends on:** `OB.PRJ.01`
- **Note:** This is the single most load-bearing modelling decision VocBench makes and the reason it can host OWL, SKOS and lexicons in one tool.

#### OB.PRJ.03 · Project settings & scoped configuration  `[MUST]` `[P0]`

Per-project settings with defaults, editable while the project is closed, some requiring a repository restart.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · Projects.setProjectProperty/getProjectPropertyMap, Settings service (17 ops)<br>**WP** · GetProjectSettings/SetProjectSettings (displayName, description, defaultLanguage, displayNameSettings, slack/webhook integration)
- **Capabilities:** B.SG.3 Policy, Standards & Conventions Management, T.OO.2 Versioning & Release Management

- **Target:** `ontology_builder.projects.settings`
- **Depends on:** `OB.PRJ.01`, `OB.EXT.02`

#### OB.PRJ.04 · Project access control list & lock levels  `[MUST]` `[P0]`

A project grants other projects (consumers) an access level (R | RW | EXT) and holds a lock level (R | W | NO); a universal ACL level applies to all consumers. Enables permission-by-delegation for cross-project alignment.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · Projects.getAccessStatus/updateAccessLevel/updateLockLevel/updateUniversalAccessLevel; models/Project.ts AccessLevel, LockLevel
- **Capabilities:** B.SG.2 Ontology Governance & Stewardship, B.SG.5 Ontology Risk & Compliance Management, T.AC.4 Ontology-based Access, APIs & Entitlements

- **Depends on:** `OB.PRJ.01`
- **Note:** Prerequisite for OB.MAP.* — you cannot align to another project's content without an ACL grant.

### GOV · Governance, Identity & Access Control

*Users, groups, roles, capabilities, project bindings and ACLs.*  ·  Backend package `ontology_builder.governance`

#### OB.GOV.01 · User accounts & registration lifecycle  `[MUST]` `[P0]`

Registration, activation (NEW | INACTIVE | ACTIVE), profile fields, password reset/force, e-mail verification, avatar, affiliation, language proficiencies, and a configurable custom-field schema.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · Users service (31 ops), models/User.ts UserForm/UserFormCustomField<br>**WP** · CreateUserAccountActionHandler, ResetPasswordActionHandler, ChangePasswordActionHandler, GetUserIdsActionHandler
- **Capabilities:** B.SG.2 Ontology Governance & Stewardship, B.CT.1 Skills & Talent Management
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.governance.users`
- **Note:** `languageProficiencies` is what makes language-restricted lexicographer roles enforceable (OB.GOV.06).

#### OB.GOV.02 · Capability expression language  `[MUST]` `[P0]`

A first-class permission grammar `auth(<area>(<subject>[,<scope>]), "<CRUDV>")` over areas rdf | pm | rbac | um | cform | customService | invokableReporter | sys, with C·R·U·D plus **V (validate)**. Evaluated identically on server and client so the UI hides what the user may not do.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · utils/AuthorizationEvaluator.ts — 330 guarded actions; areas: rdf(155) pm(17) cform(12) sys(7) invokableReporter(7) customService(7) rbac(2)<br>**WP** · BuiltInCapability — 53 flat capabilities (coarser, no CRUD algebra)
- **Capabilities:** B.SG.2 Ontology Governance & Stewardship, B.SG.3 Policy, Standards & Conventions Management, B.SG.5 Ontology Risk & Compliance Management, T.AC.4 Ontology-based Access, APIs & Entitlements
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.governance.capabilities`
- **Note:** **The single most valuable thing to port.** VocBench's algebra is strictly more expressive than WebProtégé's flat enum; adopt VB3's grammar and seed it with WP's 53 capability names where they fit.

#### OB.GOV.03 · Role definitions & role editor  `[MUST]` `[P0]`

System-level and project-level roles, each a set of capability expressions. Factory roles are immutable; user-defined roles are created per project via a wizard, cloned, exported and imported.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · Administration.createRole/cloneRole/addCapabilityToRole/updateCapabilityForRole/listCapabilities/listRoles; models/User.ts Role, RoleLevel<br>**WP** · BuiltInRole (15 roles, parent-inheriting), ProjectRoleDefinitionsManager, SetProjectRoleDefinitionsHandler

- **Depends on:** `OB.GOV.02`

#### OB.GOV.04 · Default role set  `[MUST]` `[P0]`

Ship the eight VocBench roles — Administrator (system), Project Manager, Ontology Editor, Thesaurus Editor, Lexicographer, Mapper, Validator, RDF Geek, Lurker — reconciled with WebProtégé's CanView / CanComment / CanEdit / CanManage ladder.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · §4.2 of the SWJ paper; roles_adm documentation<br>**WP** · BuiltInRole PROJECT_VIEWER→OBJECT_COMMENTER→PROJECT_EDITOR→PROJECT_MANAGER, ISSUE_VIEWER→…→ISSUE_MANAGER, SYSTEM_ADMIN/USER_ADMIN
- **Capabilities:** B.SG.2 Ontology Governance & Stewardship
- **Layers:** backend
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.governance.roles`
- **Depends on:** `OB.GOV.03`

#### OB.GOV.05 · Role inheritance  `[SHOULD]` `[P0]`

Roles compose from parent roles so the capability set is derived, not duplicated (WebProtégé's model; VocBench roles are flat).

- **Source evidence:** **WP** · BuiltInRole(parents, actions), BuiltInRoleOracle

A single `authorize(subject, capability, resource) -> bool` service used by every endpoint via a decorator, with a cached client-side twin that drives UI affordances. Emits a permissions-changed event on role/binding change.

### CHG · Change Tracking, History & Validation

*Triple-level change capture, staged commits, accept/reject workflow, undo.*  ·  Backend package `ontology_builder.changes`

#### OB.CHG.01 · Triple-level change interception  `[MUST]` `[P1]`

Every write, including raw SPARQL Update, is intercepted at the triple level and recorded as an add/remove set — not as a predefined operation type. This is what makes history complete rather than best-effort.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · §4.3 — RDF4J SAIL extension capturing effectively-modified triples into a separate *support repository*<br>**WP** · webprotege-revision-manager — axiom-level change lists
- **Capabilities:** T.OO.2 Versioning & Release Management, B.SG.2 Ontology Governance & Stewardship, B.SG.5 Ontology Risk & Compliance Management
- **Layers:** store, backend
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.changes.tracker`
- **Reuse existing:** `src/Ontology Modeler/ontology_modeler/diff.py (GraphSynchronizer)`
- **Note:** Fuseki has no SAIL. Implement as a write-path wrapper: every mutation goes through a `ChangeSet` object that computes the delta and applies it in one SPARQL Update transaction alongside the provenance write.

#### OB.CHG.02 · Commit provenance (the five Ws)  `[MUST]` `[P1]`

Each commit records actor, operation, operation parameters, start/end time, and the created/modified/deleted resources, stored as RDF.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · models/History.ts CommitInfo{commit,user,operation,operationParameters,startTime,endTime,created,modified,deleted}; History service<br>**WP** · GetRevisionSummaries, GetRevisions, RevisionSummary
- **Capabilities:** B.SG.5 Ontology Risk & Compliance Management, T.OO.2 Versioning & Release Management, T.RI.4 Inference Explainability
- **Layers:** store, backend
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.changes.provenance`
- **Depends on:** `OB.CHG.01`

#### OB.CHG.03 · History browser with delta view  `[MUST]` `[P1]`

Paged, filterable commit list (by actor, operation, time range, resource) with a per-commit additions/removals delta, truncation-aware.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · History.getCommits/getCommitSummary/getCommitDelta/getTimeOfOrigin; CommitDelta{additions,removals,additionsTruncated,removalsTruncated}<br>**WP** · ProjectHistoryPortletPresenter, GetProjectChanges, GetWatchedEntityChanges
- **Capabilities:** T.OO.2 Versioning & Release Management, B.SG.2 Ontology Governance & Stewardship
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.changes.history`
- **Depends on:** `OB.CHG.02`

#### OB.CHG.04 · Staging graphs & the validation workflow  `[MUST]` `[P1]`

When validation is enabled, edits land in `staging-add` / `staging-delete` named graphs rather than the main graph. A user holding **V** accepts (making effects permanent) or rejects (erasing them, leaving no history trace). There is no `status` property — the workflow *is* the graph layout.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · §4.4; Validation service — accept, reject, getStagedCommitSummary, getCurrentUserStagedCommitSummary, rejectCurrentUserCommit
- **Capabilities:** B.SG.2 Ontology Governance & Stewardship, B.SG.5 Ontology Risk & Compliance Management, T.QV.1 Ontology Validation (SHACL/constraints), T.OO.2 Versioning & Release Management
- **Layers:** store, backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.changes.validation`
- **Depends on:** `OB.CHG.01`, `OB.GOV.02`
- **Note:** **The keystone governance feature.** Maps cleanly onto Fuseki named graphs: <g>, <g#staging-add>, <g#staging-delete>. Read paths union main+staging and tag each triple's provenance so the UI can render proposed content distinctly.

#### OB.CHG.05 · Undo  `[SHOULD]` `[P1]`

Per-user undo of the last operation, independent of the validation workflow.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · Undo.undo; Projects.setUndoEnabled/isUndoEnabled<br>**PD** · EditMenu Undo/Redo (OWL API change-list based)
- **Capabilities:** T.OO.2 Versioning & Release Management
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.changes.undo`
- **Depends on:** `OB.CHG.01`

#### OB.CHG.06 · Revert a revision  `[SHOULD]` `[P1]`

Reverse-apply a historical commit onto the head.

- **Source evidence:** **WP** · RevertRevisionActionHandler; BuiltInCapability.REVERT_CHANGES
- **Capabilities:** T.OO.2 Versioning & Release Management
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.changes.history`
- **Depends on:** `OB.CHG.03`

#### OB.CHG.07 · Blacklisting of rejected changes  `[MAY]` `[P1]`

Remember rejected proposals so a re-proposal warns the editor. Requires validation to be enabled.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · Projects.setBlacklistingEnabled; §4.4 'future directions' now shipped
- **Capabilities:** B.SG.5 Ontology Risk & Compliance Management, T.QV.3 Quality Assurance & Metrics
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.changes.validation`
- **Depends on:** `OB.CHG.04`

#### OB.CHG.08 · Change-set safety guard  `[MUST]` `[P1]`

Before any write is applied, verify that the merged graph is a superset-preserving transformation of the base for everything the editing surface never saw — never re-serialise a lossy projection over the canonical graph.

#### OB.EDT.01 · Class authoring & taxonomy  `[MUST]` `[P2]`

Create/delete classes, add/remove superclasses, subclass navigation, instance counts.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · Classes service (17 ops) — createClass, addSuperCls, getSubClasses, getNumberOfInstances<br>**WP** · CreateClassesActionHandler, DeleteEntitiesActionHandler, GetClassFrame<br>**PD** · Add subclass/sibling/subclasses, Duplicate class, Convert to primitive/defined class
- **Capabilities:** T.DA.1 Ontology Conceptualization & Modelling, T.DA.2 Ontology Formalization (OWL/RDFS/SKOS)
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.authoring.owl.classes`
- **Depends on:** `OB.CHG.01`

#### OB.EDT.02 · Class expression axioms  `[MUST]` `[P2]`

unionOf / intersectionOf / oneOf / complementOf, general class axioms, covering axioms, disjointness (pairwise and set), equivalence.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · Classes.addUnionOf/addIntersectionOf/addOneOf + removeX<br>**PD** · 'Make primitive siblings disjoint', 'Add covering axiom', 'Split/Amalgamate disjoint classes', General class axioms view
- **Capabilities:** T.DA.2 Ontology Formalization (OWL/RDFS/SKOS), T.RI.1 Logical Consistency & Reasoning
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.authoring.owl.axioms`
- **Depends on:** `OB.EDT.01`

#### OB.EDT.03 · Manchester-syntax rendering of class expressions  `[MUST]` `[P2]`

Render any anonymous class expression as a readable Manchester-syntax string (`classifies some Role`) instead of a blank node. Read-only: a recursive walk over the restriction structure, no grammar required.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · §4.6 — Manchester syntax for visualisation of class descriptions<br>**WP** · GetManchesterSyntaxFrame<br>**PD** · 'Manchester syntax rendering' view; the Description view
- **Capabilities:** T.DA.2 Ontology Formalization (OWL/RDFS/SKOS), T.AC.2 Visualization & Exploration
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.authoring.manchester.render`
- **Note:** Measured on the local FIBO corpus (297 files, 3,190 classes): **6,388 owl:Restriction nodes** — about two anonymous expressions per named class. Without this, the majority of FIBO's semantic content renders as blank nodes and the tool is unusable against the primary corpus. ~150 lines, no dependency.

#### OB.EDT.14 · Manchester-syntax parsing & completion  `[SHOULD]` `[P6]`

Parse a typed Manchester-syntax expression into OWL axioms, with validation, precedence handling, structured parse errors and autocompletion — the free-text class-expression editor.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · ManchesterHandler service (7 ops) — checkExpression, createRestriction, updateExpression, checkDatatypeExpression; widget/codemirror/manchester-editor<br>**WP** · mansyntax/ManchesterSyntaxFrameParser wraps OWL API's ManchesterOWLSyntaxFramesParser in 6 lines; CheckManchesterSyntaxFrame, GetManchesterSyntaxFrameCompletions<br>**PD** · class expression editor with syntax checking
- **Capabilities:** T.DA.2 Ontology Formalization (OWL/RDFS/SKOS)
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.authoring.manchester.parse`
- **Depends on:** `OB.EDT.03`, `OB.EXT.05`
- **Note:** Delivered by delegating to the OWL API through the sidecar (OB.EXT.05) rather than by writing a grammar. The decisive detail is error handling: OWL API's `ParserException` exposes line, column, current token and `isClassNameExpected()` / `isObjectPropertyNameExpected()` / … — so **completion falls out of the parser for free**, which is the expensive half to build by hand. Still deferred to P6: measured, 91.2% of FIBO restrictions have a named filler and are covered by OB.EDT.15 without any parser.

#### OB.EDT.15 · Structured restriction builder  `[MUST]` `[P2]`

A three-part form — property · quantifier (some/only/value/min/max/exactly) · filler — that composes a restriction without free-text syntax, with a live Manchester-syntax preview.

- **Source evidence:** **PD** · the restriction-creation dialogs in the class Description view<br>**VB3** · ManchesterHandler.createRestriction is the server side of this
- **Capabilities:** T.DA.2 Ontology Formalization (OWL/RDFS/SKOS), T.AC.2 Visualization & Exploration
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.authoring.owl.restrictions`
- **Depends on:** `OB.EDT.03`
- **Note:** Covers the 91.2% of FIBO-shaped restrictions that have a named filler, and is far more usable than free text for non-logicians. This is what makes OB.EDT.14 deferrable rather than missing.

One universal predicate-object editor for *any* resource, organised into ~30 typed sections (types, lexicalizations, broaders, classaxioms, domains, ranges, imports, notes, members, …), each with its own CRUD authorization.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · §4.1.2; models/ResourceView.ts ResViewSection — 30 sections; AuthorizationEvaluator.sectionEvaluationMap maps every (section, CRUD) pair to a capability goal<br>**WP** · frame package (12 handlers) — GetClassFrame, GetObjectPropertyFrame, …
- **Capabilities:** T.DA.2 Ontology Formalization (OWL/RDFS/SKOS), T.AC.2 Visualization & Exploration, B.SG.2 Ontology Governance & Stewardship
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.browse.resource_view`
- **Depends on:** `OB.EDT.07`, `OB.GOV.10`
- **Note:** The centre of gravity of the whole editing UI. Its per-section CRUD authorization map is what makes fine-grained governance visible.

#### OB.BRW.04 · Inferred vs asserted rendering  `[MUST]` `[P3]`

Inferred triples are rendered distinctly and can be toggled in and out of every view.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · §4.6 and Fig. 10 — lighter colour for inferred, eye-icon toggle<br>**PD** · 'Class hierarchy (inferred)', 'Individuals by type (inferred)', 'Direct instances (inferred)', Classification results view
- **Capabilities:** T.RI.2 Inferencing & Materialization, T.RI.4 Inference Explainability, T.AC.2 Visualization & Exploration
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.browse.resource_view`
- **Depends on:** `OB.RSN.02`

#### OB.BRW.05 · Graph view  `[SHOULD]` `[P5]`

Interactive model/data/UML graph exploration with incremental expansion.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · Graph service — getGraphModel, expandGraphModelNode, expandSub/SuperResources; graph/impl/{data,model,uml}-graph<br>**WP** · viz package (4 handlers) — GetEntityGraph, SetEntityGraphActiveFilters, GetUserProjectEntityGraphCriteria<br>**PD** · OWLViz / OntoGraf plugins
- **Capabilities:** T.AC.2 Visualization & Exploration
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.browse.graph`
- **Reuse existing:** `src/Ontology Converter/ontology_to_lpg.py`

#### OB.BRW.06 · Custom trees  `[SHOULD]` `[P4]`

Define a navigable tree over arbitrary properties (not just rdfs:subClassOf or skos:broader) with a SPARQL-backed roots/children contract.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · CustomTrees service — getRoots, getChildrenResources; structures/trees/custom
- **Capabilities:** T.AC.2 Visualization & Exploration, T.DA.5 Ontology Design Pattern (ODP) Management
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.browse.custom_trees`
- **Depends on:** `OB.BRW.02`

#### OB.BRW.07 · Perspectives, portlets & saved layouts  `[SHOULD]` `[P5]`

The workspace is a user- and role-configurable arrangement of view components; layouts are savable, resettable and shippable as project defaults.

- **Source evidence:** **WP** · perspective package (7 handlers) — GetPerspectives, GetPerspectiveLayout, SetPerspectiveLayout, ResetPerspectives, SAVE_DEFAULT_PROJECT_LAYOUT; wiki 'Portlets'<br>**PD** · Window menu — Views, Tabs, 'Create new tab...', 'Export/Import tab', 'Store current layout'; 51 registered view components
- **Capabilities:** T.AC.2 Visualization & Exploration, B.VP.3 Adoption & Change Management
- **Layers:** ui, backend
- **Target:** `ontology_builder_ui/shell/perspectives`
- **Depends on:** `OB.UIX.01`
- **Note:** WebProtégé and Protégé Desktop agree on this; VocBench does not have it. It is the mechanism that lets one product serve ontologists, terminologists and reviewers without three products.

#### OB.BRW.08 · Resource-view section customisation  `[SHOULD]` `[P5]`

Per-project and per-user control over which sections appear, in what order, with filters — a template editor.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · preferences/res-view-section-customization, res-view-template-editor, section-filter-editor
- **Capabilities:** T.AC.2 Visualization & Exploration, B.VP.3 Adoption & Change Management
- **Layers:** ui, backend

### SRCH · Search & Lookup

*Lexical, prefix, advanced and custom search; path-from-root; entity lookup.*  ·  Backend package `ontology_builder.search`

#### OB.SRCH.01 · Resource search (lexical, prefix, regex, language-scoped)  `[MUST]` `[P2]`

Search over labels and IRIs with mode, language, scheme and role filters; search within instances of a class; path-from-root for reveal-in-tree.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · Search service (12 ops) — searchResource, searchPrefix, advancedSearch, searchInstancesOfClass, getPathFromRoot, searchStringList, searchURIList<br>**WP** · PerformEntitySearchActionHandler, LookupEntitiesActionHandler, GetMatchingEntitiesActionHandler, webprotege-server-lucene

#### OB.SRCH.02 · Custom search & search settings  `[SHOULD]` `[P4]`

Project-defined parameterised search services with generated input forms; stored per-user/per-project search preferences.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · Search.customSearch/getCustomSearchForm/storeCustomSearchSettings<br>**WP** · GetSearchSettings/SetSearchSettings, webprotege-criteria ('extensible criteria API for selecting entities')
- **Capabilities:** T.AC.1 Search & Query (SPARQL), T.DA.5 Ontology Design Pattern (ODP) Management

#### OB.SRCH.03 · Pluggable search strategy  `[SHOULD]` `[P4]`

The search implementation is an extension point so a store-specific full-text index can replace the portable SPARQL implementation.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · SearchStrategy extension point (§3.2)
- **Capabilities:** T.AC.1 Search & Query (SPARQL), T.OO.4 Federation & Virtualization
- **Layers:** backend
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.search.strategies`
- **Depends on:** `OB.EXT.01`

### FRM · Custom Forms & Custom Views

*Declarative, data-driven creation/visualisation forms bound to OWL properties.*  ·  Backend package `ontology_builder.forms`

#### OB.FRM.01 · Declarative custom forms  `[MUST]` `[P4]`

Data-driven definition of what is prompted when a resource of a given type is created or viewed, transforming input into arbitrary RDF — so complex design patterns are enterable by non-modellers.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · CustomForms service (24 ops) — createCustomForm, createFormCollection, addFormsMapping, getCustomFormRepresentation, removeReifiedResource; forms are PEARL templates executed by CODA (§4.1.5)<br>**WP** · form package (11 handlers) — FormDescriptor, FormFieldDescriptor, FormControlDescriptor (Text/Choice/Grid/SubForm/Collection), EntityFormChangeListGenerator, GetEntityForm, SetEntityFormsData, CopyFormDescriptorsFromProject
- **Capabilities:** T.DA.5 Ontology Design Pattern (ODP) Management, B.SE.1 Domain Knowledge Elicitation, B.VP.3 Adoption & Change Management
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.forms`
- **Note:** Two designs to choose between. WebProtégé's is a typed JSON descriptor tree with an explicit change generator — far easier to port to Python/React. VocBench's is more expressive (arbitrary RDF via PEARL) but drags in the CODA runtime. **Recommendation: adopt WebProtégé's descriptor model, add a SPARQL-CONSTRUCT escape hatch for the cases PEARL would have covered.**

#### OB.FRM.02 · Form collections & type mappings  `[MUST]` `[P4]`

Bind a form (or a collection of forms) to a class/type so it fires on creation of any instance of that type; import/export forms between projects.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · CustomForms.addFormsMapping/getFormCollection/isFormLinkedToCollection<br>**WP** · GetProjectFormDescriptors/SetProjectFormDescriptors, CopyFormDescriptorsFromProject, FormsManagerPresenter
- **Capabilities:** T.DA.5 Ontology Design Pattern (ODP) Management, B.SG.3 Policy, Standards & Conventions Management
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.forms.binding`
- **Depends on:** `OB.FRM.01`

#### OB.FRM.03 · Custom views (SPARQL-backed value widgets)  `[SHOULD]` `[P6]`

Render a predicate's values through a custom widget — map, chart, table, vector — driven by a stored query and an association to a property.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · CustomViews service (17 ops) — createCustomView, addAssociation, updateSparqlBasedData, updateDynamicVectorData; custom-views/editors/views; widget/leaflet-map, widget/charts
- **Capabilities:** T.AC.2 Visualization & Exploration, T.DA.5 Ontology Design Pattern (ODP) Management
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.forms.custom_views`
- **Depends on:** `OB.FRM.01`, `OB.SPQ.02`

#### OB.FRM.04 · Form validation & broken-form detection  `[SHOULD]` `[P4]`

Validate a form definition, infer its annotations, and report forms broken by ontology change.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · CustomForms.validatePearl/inferPearlAnnotations/getBrokenCustomForms; CODA.validatePearl
- **Capabilities:** T.QV.1 Ontology Validation (SHACL/constraints), T.QV.3 Quality Assurance & Metrics
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.forms.validation`
- **Depends on:** `OB.FRM.01`

### RSN · Reasoning & Explanation

*Consistency, classification, materialisation, entailment justification.*  ·  Backend package `ontology_builder.reasoning`

#### OB.RSN.01 · Consistency & classification  `[MUST]` `[P3]`

Run a reasoner over the project's imports closure; report unsatisfiable classes and the inferred hierarchy.

- **Source evidence:** **PD** · inference_reasonerfactory extension point, Reasoner menu, HermiT built in, Pellet/FaCT++/ELK as plugins; 'Classification results' view; DL metrics view<br>**VB3** · §4.6 — reasoning delegated to the store (RDF4J RDFS or GraphDB OWL2-RL/QL rulesets); ICV.listConsistencyViolations
- **Capabilities:** T.RI.1 Logical Consistency & Reasoning, T.QV.1 Ontology Validation (SHACL/constraints)
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.reasoning.engine`
- **Reuse existing:** `src/Ontology Enricher/src/patterns.py`
- **Note:** Python options: owlrl (OWL 2 RL, pure Python, already used in chapter04) and Fuseki's own inference cover P3 in-process. True DL classification has no Python implementation at all, so it arrives in P6 through the sidecar (OB.EXT.05) behind the same `ReasonerBackend` interface.

#### OB.RSN.02 · Materialised inference in a dedicated graph  `[MUST]` `[P3]`

Entailments are computed into a separate `inferred` named graph with a freshness stamp, never mixed into the asserted graph.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · store-level total materialisation; explicit/inferred distinction<br>Local: src/Ontology Enricher output/inferred_closure.ttl; playground-fuseki-workbench P4 design
- **Capabilities:** T.RI.2 Inferencing & Materialization, T.OO.1 Triplestore & Ontology Storage
- **Layers:** store, backend
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.reasoning.materialize`
- **Depends on:** `OB.RSN.01`, `OB.STO.01`

#### OB.RSN.03 · Explanation & justification  `[SHOULD]` `[P3]`

Human-readable justification for an inferred axiom or an inconsistency.

- **Source evidence:** **PD** · `explanation` and `inconsistentOntologyExplanation` extension points, `explanationpreferencespanel`<br>**VB3** · ICV.explain; §4.6 notes VB3 *cannot* justify because RDF4J offers no mechanism — an explicit gap this design closes
- **Capabilities:** T.RI.4 Inference Explainability, B.SG.5 Ontology Risk & Compliance Management, T.AC.6 LLM / AI Augmentation
- **Layers:** backend, agent, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.reasoning.explain`
- **Depends on:** `OB.RSN.02`
- **Note:** Protégé Desktop is the only one of the three that does this well. It is also the highest-value input to the agentic layer — an agent that can quote a justification is an agent that can be trusted. Two tiers: rule-provenance tracking under OWL 2 RL in P3 (in-process, owlrl), and true DL justifications via the sidecar (OB.EXT.05) in P6. Always show which profile produced an explanation — see decision O6.

#### OB.RSN.04 · Rule management (SHACL-AF / SWRL)  `[SHOULD]` `[P3]`

Author and execute domain rules that augment the ontology.

- **Source evidence:** **WP** · 'Rules' view is present in Protégé Desktop; WebProtégé supports SWRL rule editing (per the VB3 comparison, §6.3)<br>**PD** · Rules view (SWRLTab)<br>Local: src/Ontology Enricher catalog/reasoning_patterns.yaml
- **Capabilities:** T.RI.3 Rule & Constraint Management (SHACL/SWRL), T.DA.5 Ontology Design Pattern (ODP) Management
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.reasoning.rules`
- **Reuse existing:** `src/Ontology Enricher/catalog/reasoning_patterns.yaml`

#### OB.RSN.05 · Trivial inference toggle  `[MAY]` `[P3]`

Cheap automatic materialisation of symmetric/inverse assertions at write time, switchable per project.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · Projects.setTrivialInferenceEnabled/isTrivialInferenceEnabled
- **Capabilities:** T.RI.2 Inferencing & Materialization
- **Layers:** backend
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.reasoning.trivial`
- **Depends on:** `OB.CHG.01`

### QLT · Quality, Constraints & Testing

*SHACL, integrity-constraint validation, metrics, competency-question tests.*  ·  Backend package `ontology_builder.quality`

#### OB.QLT.01 · SHACL validation  `[MUST]` `[P3]`

Load shapes into a shapes graph, validate on demand and on commit, extract custom forms from shapes.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · SHACL service — batchValidation, clearShapes, extractCFfromShapesGraph; Projects.setSHACLValidationEnabled
- **Capabilities:** T.QV.1 Ontology Validation (SHACL/constraints), T.RI.3 Rule & Constraint Management (SHACL/SWRL), B.SG.3 Policy, Standards & Conventions Management
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.quality.shacl`
- **Note:** pySHACL covers this in Python with no sidecar.

#### OB.QLT.02 · Integrity constraint validation (ICV) with interactive fixes  `[MUST]` `[P3]`

A catalogue of ~30 model-specific anomaly checks — dangling concepts, cyclic hierarchies, hierarchical redundancy, multiple prefLabels in a language, overlapped labels, no-scheme concepts, top concepts with broaders, extra spaces in labels, invalid URIs, broken alignments, missing definitions — **each with a one-click remediation**.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · ICV service (38 ops); src/app/icv/ has one component per check
- **Capabilities:** T.QV.1 Ontology Validation (SHACL/constraints), T.QV.3 Quality Assurance & Metrics, B.SG.3 Policy, Standards & Conventions Management
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.quality.icv`
- **Note:** The interactive *fix* is the differentiator — a validation report nobody can act on is not a quality capability. Also the single best-shaped target for agent automation (OB.AGT.04).

#### OB.QLT.03 · Competency-question test suite  `[MUST]` `[P3]`

Executable tests that assert the ontology answers its competency questions; run on every change.

- **Source evidence:** Local: capability T.QV.2 has no equivalent in any of the three tools — this is an addition, drawn from architecture/ontology_assistant/EVALUATION.md
- **Capabilities:** T.QV.2 Ontology Testing (Competency-Question tests), B.SE.2 Competency Question Management, T.OO.3 Ontology CI/CD (OntoOps / DataOps)
- **Layers:** backend, agent, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.quality.cq_tests`
- **Reuse existing:** `architecture/ontology_assistant/EVALUATION.md`
- **Note:** **Gap in all three reference tools.** None of VocBench, WebProtégé or Protégé manages competency questions as first-class testable artifacts. This is where the Ontology Builder can be better than what it merges.

#### OB.QLT.04 · Quality metrics  `[SHOULD]` `[P3]`

Structural and semantic metrics — DL expressivity, axiom counts, coverage, cohesion, label completeness per language.

- **Source evidence:** **PD** · 'Ontology metrics' view, 'DL metrics' view<br>**VB3** · LIME/VoID statistical metadata computation (§4.12)
- **Capabilities:** T.QV.3 Quality Assurance & Metrics, B.VP.2 Performance Measurement (KPIs)
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.quality.metrics`
- **Reuse existing:** `src/Ontology Modeler/ontology_modeler/structure.py`

#### OB.QLT.05 · Quality gate on commit  `[MUST]` `[P3]`

A configurable policy that blocks (or routes to validation) a commit that breaks reasoning, SHACL, ICV or a CQ test.

- **Source evidence:** Composition of VB3's validation workflow with WP's revision model — not present as such in either
- **Capabilities:** T.OO.3 Ontology CI/CD (OntoOps / DataOps), T.QV.1 Ontology Validation (SHACL/constraints), B.SG.3 Policy, Standards & Conventions Management, B.SG.5 Ontology Risk & Compliance Management
- **Layers:** backend
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.quality.gate`
- **Depends on:** `OB.CHG.04`, `OB.QLT.01`, `OB.QLT.02`, `OB.QLT.03`

#### OB.QLT.06 · Invokable reporters  `[SHOULD]` `[P6]`

User-defined report definitions composed of sections, compiled on demand into HTML/Markdown — the reporting counterpart of custom services.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · InvokableReporters service (11 ops) — createInvokableReporter, addSectionToReporter, compileReport
- **Capabilities:** T.QV.3 Quality Assurance & Metrics, B.VP.2 Performance Measurement (KPIs), T.AC.3 Documentation & Publishing
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.quality.reporters`
- **Depends on:** `OB.SPQ.02`

A YASGUI-class editor with prefix autocompletion, live schema feeding, result download in tabular and RDF formats, and federation endpoint suggestion — with update guarded by capability and routed through change tracking.

#### OB.SPQ.02 · Stored & shared queries  `[SHOULD]` `[P4]`

Save a query at system/project/user scope, share it across projects, parameterise it, and pipe its graph results through a transformer chain.

Define named operations backed by parameterised SPARQL, exposed as first-class API endpoints with generated forms and their own capabilities.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · CustomServices service (12 ops) — createCustomService, addOperationToCustomService, getOperationForms, reloadCustomServices; Services service exposes the service/operation registry
- **Capabilities:** T.AC.4 Ontology-based Access, APIs & Entitlements, T.DA.5 Ontology Design Pattern (ODP) Management, B.SG.2 Ontology Governance & Stewardship

- **Depends on:** `OB.SPQ.02`, `OB.GOV.11`

#### OB.SPQ.04 · Typed programmatic API for agents & CI  `[MUST]` `[P0]`

Every backend operation is a typed function with an HTTP twin, so agents, notebooks and pipelines call the same contract the UI does.

- **Source evidence:** Local convention (bottomup_ontology.tools, ontology_assistant TOOL_CATALOG)<br>**WP** · webprotege-backend-api, Jersey REST endpoints
- **Capabilities:** T.AC.4 Ontology-based Access, APIs & Entitlements, T.OO.3 Ontology CI/CD (OntoOps / DataOps), T.AC.6 LLM / AI Augmentation

- **Target:** `ontology_builder.api`

### EXT · Extension & Configuration Framework

*Extension points, scoped settings/configurations, plugin registry.*  ·  Backend package `ontology_builder.extensions`

#### OB.EXT.01 · Extension-point registry  `[MUST]` `[P2]`

A general `component` abstraction — identifiable, configurable, scoped — and a registry of extension points that third parties implement. Ship the VocBench set: CollaborationBackend, DatasetCatalogConnector, DatasetMetadataExporter, RDFLifter, RDFTransformer, ReformattingExporter, RenderingEngine, RepositoryImplConfigurer, RepositorySourcedDeployer, RepositoryTargetingLoader, SearchStrategy, StreamSourcedDeployer, StreamTargetingLoader, URIGenerator — plus Reasoner and Matcher.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · §3.2; models/Plugins.ts ExtensionPointID (15 points), ExtensionFactory/ConfigurableExtensionFactory; Extensions service<br>**PD** · 24 OSGi extension points — EditorKitFactory, ViewComponent, WorkspaceTab, inference_reasonerfactory, searchmanager, explanation, entity_renderer, OntologyLoader, OntologyRepositoryFactory, moveaxiomskit, preferencespanel, …
- **Capabilities:** B.SG.3 Policy, Standards & Conventions Management, T.OO.3 Ontology CI/CD (OntoOps / DataOps), B.CT.3 Ecosystem & Standards Collaboration
- **Layers:** backend
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.extensions.registry`
- **Note:** In Python: entry-point groups (`ontology_builder.extensions.*`) plus a Pydantic-typed configuration schema per factory. This is the architectural decision that determines whether the Builder can grow without forking — take VocBench's design wholesale.

#### OB.EXT.02 · Scoped settings & stored configurations  `[MUST]` `[P0]`

Settings and configurations exist at SYSTEM, PROJECT, USER, PROJECT_USER, PROJECT_GROUP and FACTORY scope with defaults cascading down; any extension's configuration can be stored, named, shared and reused.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · models/Plugins.ts Scope enum; Settings service (17 ops) with getSettingsDefault/storePUSettingProjectDefault/getSettingsScopes; Configurations service (7 ops)
- **Capabilities:** B.SG.3 Policy, Standards & Conventions Management, B.CT.2 Knowledge Sharing & Community of Practice
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.extensions.settings`
- **Note:** Needed in P0 because project settings, rendering and URI generation all sit on it.

#### OB.EXT.03 · Auto-generated configuration UI  `[MUST]` `[P4]`

Settings schemas render themselves as forms in the client, so a new extension needs no front-end work.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · §3.2 — 'the user interface is informed by the extension point mechanism and supports extensions with automatically built forms'; widget/settings-renderer, widget/extension-configurator
- **Capabilities:** B.SG.3 Policy, Standards & Conventions Management, T.AC.2 Visualization & Exploration
- **Layers:** ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder_ui/components/SettingsRenderer`
- **Depends on:** `OB.EXT.02`
- **Note:** Pydantic/JSON-Schema → React form generator. This is what keeps the React layer from becoming the bottleneck on backend extensibility.

#### OB.EXT.04 · UI extension slots  `[SHOULD]` `[P8]`

Named slots in the React shell (structure tabs, resource-view sections, value renderers, tools menu) that plugins register into at runtime.

- **Source evidence:** **PD** · ViewComponent / WorkspaceTab / EditorKitMenuAction extension points — the capability VocBench explicitly lacks ('provisioning of arbitrary extensions for the user interface … is still missing in VB3, due to limitations of the Angular technology', §6.3)
- **Capabilities:** T.AC.2 Visualization & Exploration, B.CT.3 Ecosystem & Standards Collaboration
- **Layers:** ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder_ui/shell/slots`
- **Depends on:** `OB.BRW.07`
- **Note:** React module federation makes this practical in a way Angular did not for VocBench — a place where the merged product can beat both predecessors.

#### OB.EXT.05 · OWL API sidecar service  `[SHOULD]` `[P6]`

A single stateless JVM service, behind HTTP and behind Python interfaces, giving the platform the Java OWL tooling that has no Python equivalent: Manchester-syntax parsing/rendering/completion (OWL API), DL classification and justifications (HermiT / ELK + OWL Explanation), and optionally ROBOT for release operations.

- **Source evidence:** **WP** · webprotege-robot-service — 'Spring Boot service wrapping ROBOT for programmatic ontology processing and manipulation in WebProtege'; the precedent for reaching Java OWL tooling from a service architecture<br>**PD** · the `inference_reasonerfactory`, `explanation` and `inconsistentOntologyExplanation` extension points — note that Protege core ships only NoOpReasoner; HermiT arrives via protege-distribution
- **Capabilities:** T.RI.1 Logical Consistency & Reasoning, T.RI.4 Inference Explainability, T.DA.2 Ontology Formalization (OWL/RDFS/SKOS), T.OO.3 Ontology CI/CD (OntoOps / DataOps)
- **Layers:** backend
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.sidecar (Python client) + services/owl-sidecar (Java)`
- **Depends on:** `OB.RSN.01`
- **Note:** Justified by serving **two** unrelated gaps at once, not one. Pin the OWL API version explicitly — WebProtege is on 4.5.13, Protege Desktop on 4.5.29, and 5.x has incompatible packages. Costs to accept: a JVM in the deployment, cold start, a serialization boundary on a keystroke-latency path, and the entity-resolution round trip (solve with a per-project name->IRI dictionary cached in the sidecar and invalidated by change events, as WebProtege does with DictionaryManager).

### S2R · Structured-Source Lifting

*Spreadsheet/DB → RDF lifting with a declarative projection language.*  ·  Backend package `ontology_builder.lifting`

#### OB.S2R.01 · Spreadsheet & database lifting  `[SHOULD]` `[P6]`

Load a sheet or a JDBC/SQL source, inspect headers, map each header to a node/graph application, preview generated triples, then commit them.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · Sheet2RDF service (31 ops) — getSheetHeaders, updateSubjectHeader, addAdvancedGraphApplicationToHeader, getTriplesPreview, addTriples, uploadDBInfo, getSupportedDBDrivers<br>**WP** · csv package — ImportCSVFileActionHandler, GetCSVGridActionHandler; cellfie-plugin for Protégé Desktop
- **Capabilities:** T.DA.4 Bottom-up Ontology Learning, T.IA.3 Semantic Data Integration, B.SE.1 Domain Knowledge Elicitation
- **Layers:** backend, ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.lifting.sheet`
- **Reuse existing:** `bottomup_ontology/`
- **Note:** All three tools have a version of this; VocBench's is by far the most complete. It is also the natural landing zone for the existing `bottomup_ontology` pipeline (T.DA.4).

#### OB.S2R.02 · Text-to-ontology bottom-up pipeline  `[SHOULD]` `[P7]`

Text cleaning → pre-processing → term extraction → relation extraction → axiom finding → human-in-the-loop → evaluation, producing candidate classes, properties and constraints.

- **Source evidence:** Local: bottomup_ontology/ (Keet Ch.7 Fig. 7.7) — already implemented as a networkx DiGraph of agent-callable steps<br>**VB3** · CODA is designed for exactly this but 'has not yet been exploited inside VB3' (§3.4) — an explicit gap this design fills
- **Capabilities:** T.DA.4 Bottom-up Ontology Learning, B.SE.1 Domain Knowledge Elicitation, T.QV.4 Verification & Evaluation (gold standard)
- **Layers:** backend, agent
- **Target:** `ontology_builder.lifting.text`
- **Depends on:** `OB.CHG.04`
- **Reuse existing:** `bottomup_ontology/`
- **Note:** Its output must land in the staging graphs, never the main graph — candidate axioms are proposals by construction.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · widget/codemirror/{manchester,turtle,ntriple,pearl,json,html,mustache}-editor, widget/pickers/*, lang-string-editor, typed-literal-input
- **Capabilities:** T.DA.2 Ontology Formalization (OWL/RDFS/SKOS), T.AC.5 Multilingual & Localization Support
- **Layers:** ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder_ui/components/editors`
- **Depends on:** `OB.EDT.03`, `OB.SPQ.01`

#### OB.UIX.06 · Localisation of the application itself  `[SHOULD]` `[P5]`

The UI is translated, independently of the data's languages.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · src/assets/l10n/
- **Capabilities:** T.AC.5 Multilingual & Localization Support, B.VP.3 Adoption & Change Management
- **Layers:** ui
- **Target:** `ontology_builder_ui/i18n`

#### OB.UIX.07 · Branding & content customisation  `[MAY]` `[P5]`

Configurable home page, navbar brand, footer — so a deployment can be presented as the organisation's own ontology portal.

- **Source evidence:** **VB3** · CustomContent service — setHomeContent, setNavbarBrandContent, setFooterContent
- **Capabilities:** B.VP.3 Adoption & Change Management
- **Layers:** ui, backend
- **Target:** `ontology_builder_ui/shell/branding`

## 4. Gaps in all three reference platforms

Features with no reference-tool evidence — where the merged product must be better than everything it merges:

| Feature | Why none of the three has it |
|---|---|
| **OB.CHG.08** Change-set safety guard | Already built and live-verified against the 133k-triple Fuseki dataset; lift it verbatim into the Builder. |
| **OB.STO.04** Derived property-graph projection | Keep FalkorDB in step with Fuseki as a *derived* projection for fast neighbourhood, similarity and path queries — never as a source of truth. |
| **OB.QLT.03** Competency-question test suite | **Gap in all three reference tools.** None of VocBench, WebProtégé or Protégé manages competency questions as first-class testable artifacts. This is where the Ontology Builder can be better than what it merges. |
| **OB.QLT.05** Quality gate on commit | A configurable policy that blocks (or routes to validation) a commit that breaks reasoning, SHACL, ICV or a CQ test. |
| **OB.MAP.06** Mappings in a dedicated named graph | All cross-ontology mappings are written to a separate mapping graph, never into the source ontologies. |
| **OB.AGT.01** Agent tool surface over the typed API | Every backend operation is exposed as a typed, individually testable agent tool with declared read/write intent and required capability. |
| **OB.AGT.02** Ontology Assistant (read-only comprehension agent) | Answers questions about what the ontology asserts, with citations, using the Falkor-proposes / Fuseki-proves retrieval funnel and a grounding critic. |
| **OB.AGT.03** Authoring copilot (proposal-only) | **The governance keystone applied to AI.** Because the validation workflow already exists, an LLM is just another editor whose work requires the V capability to land. No new trust model is needed. |
| **OB.AGT.06** Competency-question agent | Elicits and maintains competency questions from stakeholder text, synthesises SPARQL tests from them, and reports coverage. |
| **OB.AGT.07** Governance & stewardship agent | Watches the validation queue and the change history; surfaces stale proposals, unassigned stewardship, policy drift and capability-model maturity gaps against the EKGF target level. |
| **OB.AGT.08** Agent evaluation harness | A gold set of competency questions, retrieval and faithfulness metrics, and a regression harness run in CI for every agent. |
